subject: Business Models
title: Razor and Blade
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Razor and Blade.

hook.text: King Gillette gave away razors in 1904 and made a fortune on replacement blades. The model persists everywhere.

buildup.text: Sell the base product cheap (or free). Lock customers in. Profit from ongoing consumable purchases.

discovery.text: Printers, Keurig, game consoles, and electric toothbrushes all use razor-blade economics.

twist.text: Dollar Shave Club reversed it: cheap blades, direct to consumer. It sold to Unilever for $1 billion.

climax.text: Razor-blade is powerful but vulnerable. Cheap alternatives can break the consumable lock-in.

punchline.text: Free razor, expensive blades since 1904. 120 years later, the model still works.

quiz.question: How did Dollar Shave Club disrupt the razor-blade model?
options: Cheaper blades sold directly to consumers
